title: BBC News - Breaking news, video and the latest top stories from the U.S. and around the world
content:
People are being urged to stay alert, with earthquake aftershocks potentially reaching magnitude 7, officials say

US Central Command says proxy groups launched attacks against US bases and Saudi energy infrastructure.

The former top US health official is invoking his right to remain silent as senators grill him under oath about the pandemic.

Hansard, who was 56, won the best song Oscar for the 2007 low-budget musical film Once.

The actor and musician faces allegations from 10 women in total who say he mistreated them as teenagers.

Spain and France are both braced for the start of the fourth heatwave so far this summer and some fires have continued to burn.

All seven members of the band post a statement online, saying they will boycott the 2027 ceremony.

From "delulu" to "FOMO", Gen Z slang has made an unlikely journey from Instagram to parliament.

At least 13 people have been killed after the earthquake struck the island of Kyushu on Tuesday.

Video shows locations across the region where a strong earthquake struck Japan's Kyushu island on 28 July.

Japan is reeling from a major earthquake that hit Kyushu island. Here is what we know so far.

The Nippon Paper Industries factory in Kumamoto suffered significant damage.

Staff in the newsroom ducked beneath their desks as the earthquake struck on Tuesday afternoon.

West Africa is becoming increasingly attractive to those who want to make and export illicit drugs.

More young couples are now signing prenups to set out who gets what in the event of divorce.

Campaign group Electrical Safety First has urged those "heading abroad this summer to think before they buy".

A home on the edge of al-Mughayyir has become a weekly frontline in the battle for the occupied West Bank.

It is the highest number of elephant deaths to be recorded in this area of southern Kenya in decades.

The drought declarations follow an exceptionally hot and dry period, which has hit rivers, crops and nature.

The 16-year-old lifeguard rescued a 10-year-old who had been swept offshore at a California beach.

The two leaders sound encouraged after holding back-to-back bilaterals at the White House.

The report also says 2025 was the deadliest year for Jews living outside Israel in more than 30 years.

The US and China are locked in a race to the lead the world in robotics and artificial intelligence.

Jay Clayton's confirmation comes after the US president's original choice was rejected by lawmakers due to lack of relevant experience

The massive outage has left homes, businesses and some essential services severely disrupted.

Fifa has set a deadline of 19 September for member associations to access cash as FA voice disapproval of world governing body's funding plan before emergency Uefa meeting.

Formula 1 president Stefano Domenicali says the 2026 championship will end in Europe if the conflict in the Middle East makes it impossible to hold the season-closing races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

Follow live text updates from day six of the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

Brighton striker Danny Welbeck is given permission to have a medical at Stamford Bridge as his switch to Chelsea moves closer.

Tottenham manager Roberto de Zerbi says he has told midfielder Lucas Bergvall to stay but cannot promise him a starting role.

Yan Diomande has quickly gone from being a relatively unknown winger to the brink of becoming Real Madrid's record signing.

Fifa's plans to seek private investment in its major competitions - including the World Cup - has caused outrage within the FA and Uefa.
